A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniRe and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E. Shared methods and experiments can be reliably matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original Waymo reconstruction, novel-view synthesis and LiDAR evaluations, component ablations, and additional 32-scene results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds comparative evaluations under crowded, nighttime, adverse-weather and highway conditions.

M1.justification: The Gaussian scene graph, SMPL and shared deformation components, rendering procedure and joint optimization remain unchanged. Section 4.2's tracklet notation restates existing IoU matching and pose interpolation. Omitting the separate scene-pose alignment explanation does not establish that the underlying procedure changed.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds explicit Waymo evaluations under extreme crowding, nighttime illumination, rainy/foggy/cloudy weather and highway conditions. Section 5 also reports extensions to NuScenes, Argoverse2, PandaSet, KITTI and NuPlan, although their results are directed outside the PDFs. The 32-scene Waymo evaluation already existed in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched appearance, geometry, 32-scene and ablation comparisons. The new challenge tables reuse DeformableGS, PVG and StreetGS. The newly discussed concurrent work by Fischer et al. (2024a) is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: New challenge evaluations specify three crowded, three nighttime, seven adverse-weather and three highway scenes; highway human metrics are marked inapplicable. Existing evaluation protocols retain every-tenth-frame testing, the camera resolution, PSNR/SSIM and geometry metrics, and the 30,000-iteration training budget.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.3 systematically tests performance under dense occlusion, low light, adverse weather and high-speed driving, with four comparative tables. This substantially expands robustness analysis beyond v1's component ablations. Existing SMPL, pose refinement, bounding-box refinement and AbsGrad analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for these evaluations. The additional tables retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All matched numerical tables retain their values. New Tables 7–10 add substantial results: crowded-scene reconstruction PSNR is 31.25 for OmniRe versus PVG's 29.11; highway full-image NVS PSNR is 28.01 versus StreetGS's 28.05. Nighttime vehicle NVS also favors StreetGS, 24.61 versus 24.29. These are new-condition results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Rendering, Gaussian transformations, SMPL operations and loss definitions are mathematically unchanged. The new tracklet sets and matching/completion functions in Section 4.2 formalize previously described operations without adding substantive assumptions, derivations, guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 adds a headline claim of demonstrated generalizability across six driving datasets. Core reconstruction, controllability and state-of-the-art claims, including the stated PSNR margins, remain unchanged. Human-centered simulation receives greater emphasis, but its capabilities were already described and illustrated in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix D.3 adds interpretations of robustness and explains highway parity with StreetGS through the absence of non-rigid actors. The limitations retain lighting, distant-view and label-dependence concerns; v2 additionally proposes joint camera-pose optimization as a future mitigation for novel-view limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct code-repository link, identifiers for the challenge scenes and more explicit camera/tracklet indexing. It removes v1's explanation of correcting human-pose scale and position using bounding boxes. Appendix A's initialization, hyperparameters, loss weights, GPU and training-time disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges concurrent non-rigid modeling by Fischer et al. (2024a), distinguishing its lack of fine-grained human control. It adds dataset, tracking and simulator references and removes several human-capture references. The central positioning relative to scene graphs and human reconstruction remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around digital twins and human-centered simulation. Section 4.2 becomes an expanded tracklet-based exposition, preliminary equations are condensed into prose, ethics becomes a separate numbered section, and acknowledgements are added. Author-year citations replace numbered citations throughout.

P2.justification: v2 adds four challenge-comparison tables and broadly reformats typography and display placement. Figure 3 receives revised labels and mathematical annotations; v1's main-text simulation Figure 8 moves to the appendix as Figure 9, and other displays are relocated. Most existing result imagery and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new challenge comparisons strengthen robustness evidence beyond v1's already substantial Waymo evaluation and reveal where OmniRe's advantage becomes small. These gains are tempered by the absence of in-PDF results for the newly claimed five-dataset extension and the reduced scene-pose alignment documentation. Overall, the revision provides a useful but bounded quality improvement.
